name: Week 18 Push — Steady State (Spotlight: Dips + Cable Block)
description: Volume and loads hold. The light Kinesis-fly opener stays in the warmup so the chest moves through full range before pressing. Spotlights cycle forward to dips — now settled enough to earn the deep-cue treatment — and the cable block, which gets a cue refresh and lists per-equipment numbers (column / rope pulley / Kinesis) after W17's whole block ran on the pulley. The presses hold at 45: the W17 read was that fuller rest, not lighter load, is what recovers the set-3 reps. Push press runs first when the rack's free.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state — sets and loads hold; the work is rest discipline + depth of execution. Light Kinesis-fly opener stays in the warmup. Spotlight cycles to dips (settled in, deep cues now) + the cable block (cue refresh + per-equipment numbers). Push press runs first, fresh; fuller rest is the lever to recover the set-3 reps. Dips stay bodyweight, fuller ROM (the shoulder tolerated it W17); watch the front pec stays pressure, not pain.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — dips debuted clean W17 (bodyweight 12/(6+6)/8, full ROM, no shoulder complaint), so they earn the deep-cue treatment now. Spotlight drills the lean-forward chest-bias, the pack-down at the top, and the front-pec-pressure-not-pain watch so the new pattern grooves without waking the at-risk shoulder.

Cycles forward as the cable-block refresh — W17's whole cable block ran on the rope pulley (column was taken), so the block gets sharper cues and per-equipment numbers. Spotlight drills the fixed-hinge, lats-to-the-thighs pull and the front-pec-quiet setup that backed 57.5 down to a clean 50 on the pulley.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W16 lateral raise + Kinesis fly · W17 push press + incline DB · W18 dips + cable block (current) · W19 cycle forward — push press + lateral raise refresh.
watchpoints: **Rest is the lever, not load.** W17 showed the set-3 fades come from short rest (push press dropped to 8 on ~30s rest; incline finished when rested longer). Take the prescribed ~2 min on the presses — expect the reps to hold. Don't drop weight to chase a feeling that fuller rest fixes.

**Light Kinesis-fly opener stays in the warmup** — a few easy, light tree-hugger reps to open the chest before pressing (same logic as warming up before squats). It primes, it doesn't fatigue. Working Kinesis fly is still later in the day.
**Run push press first when the rack's free** — fresh shoulders; the heavy overhead lift wants no pre-fatigue.

**Dips spotlight — bodyweight, fuller ROM is fine now.** The shoulder tolerated full depth W17 with no complaint; keep going deep, chest-bias / lean-forward, pack down. Watch the **front pec stays 'pressure,' not pain** — if it tips to pain, shorten the depth or move to the supported machine.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — push press, lateral raise, incline DB, dips, farmer carry all carry the cue. A lockout that needs a shrug = the load's too heavy for the cue.

**Cable block lists per-equipment numbers (column / rope pulley / Kinesis)** — pick what's free, log the equipment + number. After W17 the pulley numbers are known: tri ext ~35, straight-arm pulldown 50, lateral raise (reg-pulley d-handle) 10.
**Day is at capacity** — W17 ran long and left you wiped. No adds; this is the full menu.

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Chest Opener + Pull-Up Greasing + Protective Shrug

exercises.notes: Slow, big circles. Wake up scap glide before loading.
Full sequence with red band. Non-negotiable on push day.

**Light loosening opener — NOT a working set** (the working fly comes later). On the Kinesis, light load: 'hug a tree' forward, then let the cables pull the arms open into the pec stretch. The cable holds tension in the stretched position, so it actively opens the chest before pressing. Quick and easy; this primes, it doesn't fatigue.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — dials a stretch up the back chain from forearm to shoulder. Wakes the grip and shoulder line before loading.
Ribs down, glutes tight, body in one line. Slow eccentric, 1s pause with chest 1-2" off the floor.

**Pull-up greasing set.** 1 fresh set, slow tempo, NOT to failure. Active hang start, pull elbows down to ribs, chest leads. Frequency, not max effort — drop to scapular-pulls only if the shoulder talks, and finish the count.

**Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set, DBs held behind the body, palms back. Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down. The 'opposite movement' that decompresses the right shoulder — costs no time, easy to forget.

sets.name: Push Press (3 Sets at 45 — Run First, Rest Full)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb DBs per side. 3 sets of 8-10. Run first when the rack's open.
- **Rest the full ~2 min between sets** — W17 set 3 fell to 8 on ~30s rest; with full rest it holds 10. The rest is the fix, not a lighter bell.
- **Ribs DOWN before the dip** — catch any rib flare on set 1
- **Shallow dip ~3-4"**, straight down through the heels — the drive comes from the legs
- **Vertical DB path** — DBs travel up next to the ears, head pokes through at the top
- **Pack DOWN, not up** at the lockout — if it needs a shrug, the load's too heavy for the cue
- **Hybrid tempo:** explosive drive up, controlled descent.

**LOAD:** 15lb DBs. 3 sets of 15-18.
- **Targets the medial (side) deltoid** — the slow eccentric maxes time-under-tension on a small muscle, which is why the last set stays hard even at 15
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the wrist follows the elbow, the hand never lifts first
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED** through the whole rep
- **Stop at shoulder height — never higher** (higher just shrugs the traps off the medial delt)
- **2s eccentric** — the slow descent is the stimulus
- **Scap reset between sets** — roll the shoulders, engage/disengage the scapula a few times; this is what's kept the right shoulder quiet here.

sets.name: Incline DB Press (3 Sets at 45 pair — Rest Full)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb pair. 3 sets — fast-up / controlled-down, 1s pause at the bottom.
- **Rest the full ~2 min** — W17 the last set completed once rested longer ('rest helps apparently'). 12 reps is the hypertrophy range by design; let the rest keep each set quality.
- **Bench at 30°**, not 45° — steeper biases front delt over upper chest
- **Shoulders packed back AND down** — pin the back of the shoulder into the bench, hold it the whole set
- **Forearm stacked vertically over the elbow at the bottom** — keeps the load off the front of the shoulder
- **Elbows ~45° from torso**, not flared to 90°
- **1s pause at the bottom**, press to a fingerwidth apart at the top.

**LOAD / EQUIPMENT (pick by how the shoulder feels, log which):**
- **Bodyweight parallel-bar dips** (default) — 3 sets of 8-12
- **Supported / assisted dip machine** if the front shoulder talks — same movement, just enough assist to keep the depth controlled
- **Band-assisted** if the machine's taken

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the chest-bias dip, now grooving:**
- **Lean the torso forward ~15-30° and let the elbows flare slightly** — that's what shifts the load onto the chest (upright + tucked = triceps-bias)
- **Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK at the top** — never shrug up around the ears; pack-down is the whole game on dips
- **Fuller ROM is fine now** — W17 you went full depth with no shoulder complaint, so keep going deep, controlled
- **Controlled descent ~2s, drive up to a soft lockout** — don't drop into the bottom or snap the elbows at the top
- **Front-pec watch:** a little pressure on the front pec at the bottom stretch is expected (chest-bias dip). If it tips from 'pressure' to PAIN, shorten the depth or move to the supported machine — that's the cue, not the rep count
- **Body-bob settles with reps** — keep the feet folded behind, brace the core to stop the swing

**Reflection:** does the front pec stay 'pressure' (fine) through all three sets, and the shoulder stay quiet — or does the pec tip to pain / the shoulder start talking by set 3? Quiet shoulder is the win; if it talks, supported machine + shorter range, don't push through.

**LOAD:** Kinesis 9 (drop to 8 only if 9 feels off on set 1).
- **Slight forward hinge at the hips** — chest leads, not the head
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — these are NOT presses; the elbow angle never changes
- **'Hug a tree'** — the squeeze comes from the chest, not the arms pulling together
- **Stop a fistwidth apart at the top** — don't crash the handles
- **Slow eccentric (~3s)** — let the cables pull the arms into the deep pec stretch; the right shoulder/pec reads this loaded stretch as relief, protect that.

sets.name: 🔆 Cable Block — Lat Raise → Tri Ext → Straight-Arm Pulldown (Refresh + Per-Equipment Numbers, 3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick what's free, log which):**
- **Cable column: 30** (the pain-free home)
- **Regular pulley, D-handle at ankle height: 10** (W17 — 'felt about the same as cable column')
- **Kinesis: 5-6**

3 rounds, one arm at a time.
- **Lead with the elbow as a DIRECTION** — the elbow points, doesn't bend
- **Soft elbow ~10°, FIXED** throughout
- **Stand sideways** to the stack, working arm farther from it
- **Stop at shoulder height — higher = traps**
- **2s eccentric**, fight the cable down.

**LOAD (pick what's free, log which):**
- **Cable column: 70** (default)
- **Rope pulley: ~35** (W17 — 30 was too easy, 35 'died at 10')
- **Kinesis: 5**

3 rounds. **Always kneeling — there's no bench at this station; the forward torso lean IS the 'incline.'**
- **Kneel facing AWAY from the high pulley**, rope overhead
- **Elbows PINNED** — only the forearms move
- **Hands shoulder-width on the rope**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the rope pull the hands behind the head
- **Stop just shy of lockout**, slow eccentric. Set 1 feels easy, set 3 is brutal — that's the lift working.

**LOAD (pick what's free, log which):**
- **Cable column: 120** (the column working number)
- **Rope pulley: 50** (W17 — 57.5 was 'insanely hard' + woke the front pec, 50 was the clean working weight)
- **Kinesis: 6**

3 rounds. **🔆 SPOTLIGHT — fixed hinge, lats to the thighs:**
- **Stand a step back, hinge ~15° at the hips** — fixed hinge, the torso doesn't pump
- **Slight elbow bend (~5°), FIXED throughout**
- **Pull the bar to the thighs, NOT past** — past = shoulders roll forward, lats switch off (this is also where the front pec gets pulled into it; keep it short)
- **Squeeze the lats hard at the bottom** — 'oranges into the back pockets'
- **Slow controlled return to a full overhead stretch.** Runs last after both presses — reps may fall on the later sets; that's the load and the fatigue, both honest.

**Reflection:** does the work stay in the lats with the front pec quiet, or does the pec start taking over (the W17 57.5 signal)? If the pec lights up, the load's too high for the line of pull — back it down, like 57.5 → 50 on the pulley.

sets.notes: Cable block — sharp cues, 3 rounds, one trip to the chosen station covers all three. Per-equipment numbers listed (column is the default; the pulley numbers are from W17 when the column was taken). Pick what's free and log it.

sets.name: Farmer Carry (3 Walks)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb DBs. 3 walks of ~45-60s each — chase hold-time.
- **Stand TALL** — ribs down, crown reaching up, no leaning back
- **Shoulders pulled DOWN and BACK** — into the back pockets, never shrugged. The DBs pull the shoulders up the whole walk; resist the whole walk. This tall, packed posture doubles as right-shoulder decompression — it reads as relief.
- **Neck long, eyes forward** — no chin poke
- **Grip firm but NOT death-clenched** — grip is the limiter here (it taps before the shoulder); set the bells down when grip fails rather than white-knuckling
- **Walk a straight line at a deliberate pace**, breathing steadily.

sets.notes: Trap-chain + grip block. 3 walks at 50lb — packed-shoulder posture, grip as the honest edge. Set them down when grip gives, not before.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen — the antagonist to the upper-trap chain loaded all session.
Passive hang from the pull-up bar. **Don't engage** — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side on the mat. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Front leg + back leg at 90°. Sink the hips toward the floor — hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift before leaving the gym.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Rest is the lever** — take the full ~2 min on push press + incline DB; W17 showed the set-3 fades are under-rest, not load. Don't drop weight.
**Light Kinesis-fly opener in the warmup** — open the chest before pressing; keep it light, it primes not fatigues.
**Spotlight: dips + cable block.** Dips drill the chest-bias lean + pack-down + front-pec-pressure-not-pain watch (fuller ROM is fine now); the cable block gets a cue refresh + per-equipment numbers.
**Run push press first when the rack's free** — fresh shoulders.
**Dips stay bodyweight, fuller ROM** — the shoulder tolerated full depth W17; supported machine the moment the front shoulder (not pec) talks.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — every press + the carry carries the cue.
**Cable block per-equipment numbers** — column 30/70/120; rope pulley 10(reg, lat raise)/35/50; Kinesis 5-6. Pick what's free, log it.
**Farmer carry: 50lb, chase hold-time** — grip is the edge; the tall packed posture relieves the right shoulder.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
**Day is at capacity** — no adds; W17 already ran long. Rest: 2 min push press + dips + incline, 90s lateral raise + Kinesis fly + farmer carry, 75s cable block.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state push week — the gains come from rest discipline and sharper execution at established loads, not heavier bells. W17's lesson bakes in: fuller rest recovers the reps, so the presses hold 45 and rest full. Dips graduate to spotlight now that they've proven shoulder-friendly — drilled as chest-bias, pack-down, fuller-ROM work with the front pec watched. The cable block gets its per-equipment map so a taken column never derails the session. Building decades, not weeks.
